title: Sample: first call with Hongsheng Technology
context: Hongsheng Technology · first discovery call · counterpart: Mr. Lin, procurement manager. Their support line misses most evening calls; a competitor's voice system failed last year.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Good afternoon Mr. Lin, thanks for making time. To start, roughly how many calls does your support team take a day?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: In peak season three hundred or more, normally around two hundred. The real headache is nobody answers after eight in the evening, so every morning starts with a pile of voicemails.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Understood, so the missed evening calls are the biggest pain point. What share of those calls are repetitive things like order status?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Sixty percent at least. Has it shipped, when will the invoice be issued, that kind of thing.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: That part we can connect straight to your ERP, so a caller gives an order number and gets the answer. During the day we filter first and route the ones that need a person to your team.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Sounds good. But we trialed another vendor's system last year. Customers hung up the moment they heard a machine, so we shut it down.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: That's a fair concern. Our approach is to say up front that a human is one request away. Across our deployments only about fifteen percent of callers ask to transfer. I can send you that data.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Yes, I want to see that number. And pricing? My boss will ask about that first.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: For your volume, setup is about one hundred fifty thousand, then thirty thousand a month, which covers maintenance and two thousand minutes of calls.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Thirty thousand a month is on the high side. Last year's vendor was eighteen.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: I understand. The difference is the live ERP integration and the human handoff, which last year's vendor didn't have. If we start with evenings only, the monthly fee comes down to about twenty two thousand so you can validate first.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Twenty two I can take to my boss. But we need to see a demo first, and Mr. Wang from IT has to be there.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Of course. Does next Wednesday afternoon work? I'll prepare a demo recorded with your most common questions.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Next Wednesday at three works. One more thing, where is the data stored? Some of our customer data can't leave the country.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Let me confirm the hosting location when I'm back, and I'll give you a written answer before the demo.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Thank you Mr. Lin. I'll email the deployment data and the quote before end of day, and see you next Wednesday.

What did I commit to in this call, with what deadlines? Did he ask anything I didn't answer?
Given why last year's vendor failed, what should my demo next Wednesday address?
